useCase.name: Open the books and read them, tracing any entry back to what caused it
useCase.featureRef: 4.18 Reading the books: ledger, trial balance and journals

intent.name: finance.ledger.read
intent.summary: Read an account's ledger over a period — every entry, both sides, and the running balance. One step, and nothing is posted.
routesHere: show me the bank account ledger for September

routesHere.text: fee income account mein September mein kya aaya?
routesHere.gloss: what came into the fee income account in September?

routesHere.text: is account ka balance kya hai?

routesHere: open the late fee income ledger for the year

request.gloss: where did this entry come from?

routesElsewhere.note: No entry is ever edited or deleted. A correction is a voucher or one of the reversal use cases, never a change to a line in the ledger (BR-5).
Nothing is posted here. Entries arrive because something else happened (BR-4).

steps.note: One step. Every amount is calculated from the entries already posted — nothing is typed here (BR-2, BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A missing chart of accounts, an empty range and a range longer than the system will render are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors or as empty results.
plan.atomicity: A read that writes one thing: an audit entry, because the ledger carries the school's whole financial position (BR-11). Nothing is posted, edited or deleted (BR-4, BR-5). A closed period is readable but not postable — reading history is always permitted (BR-9).

operations.name: finance.ledger.read
operations.purpose: Return an account's entries over a period with both sides and a running balance in date order.

parameters.name: account_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such account in the chart of accounts.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with account code and name.

parameters.notes: An account from the chart of accounts. No feature creates one, and it must exist before anything here can be read (BR-1, E1).

parameters.name: date_from
parameters.notes: The start of the period. Within the financial year, or spanning several (BR-10).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The account's entries and its position.

fields.name: account_name
fields.description: From the chart of accounts.

fields.name: opening_balance
fields.description: The balance at the start of the range.

fields.name: entries
fields.description: date, debit, credit, running_balance, source — never typed (BR-2, BR-7).

fields.name: closing_balance
fields.description: At the end of the range.

fields.name: produced_at
fields.description: When the figure was produced, so a number quoted an hour later can be dated (BR-8).

fields.name: period_closed
fields.description: True where the range falls in a closed period — readable, not postable (BR-9).

fields.name: financial_year
fields.description: The year the ledger runs against, which is not the academic session (BR-10).

errors.note: No feature in the specification creates one. The books cannot be read until it exists (BR-1).

errors.meaning: The date range spans no posted entry.
errors.written: The audit entry for the read.
errors.note: The opening balance is still returned. An answer, not a failure.

errors.meaning: The range is longer than the system will render at once.
errors.note: Narrow the range. Narrowing is the actor's choice.

errors.meaning: The date falls before the financial year begins.

operations.writesOnRead: Reading the ledger writes an audit entry naming the actor and the time, because these figures carry the school's whole financial position (BR-11).

planningRules.rule: Never compute a balance. Every figure comes from the entries posted, with the running balance in date order (BR-2, BR-7) — a total worked out in a reply is a second set of books.
Never offer to post, edit or delete an entry. Nothing is posted here, and no entry is ever edited or deleted anywhere (BR-4, BR-5) — a correction is a voucher or a reversal use case.
Quote every figure with its produced_at. A trial balance or a balance quoted in a meeting an hour later has to be datable (BR-8).
Report a closed period as readable but not postable. Reading history is always permitted; changing it is not (BR-9).

Never confuse the financial year with the academic session. The ledger runs against a financial year, which is not necessarily the academic session and is defined nowhere in the specification (BR-10).

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse. The audit entry it writes is deliberate and never editable.

request.text: bank account ka September ka ledger dikhao
request.gloss: show the bank account ledger for September

resolvedPlans.outcome: Opening balance, every entry with both sides and a running balance in date order, and the closing balance — each with produced_at (PR-3). Every entry names its source, so any of them can be traced.

request.text: fee income account ka saal bhar ka dikhao
request.gloss: show the fee income account for the whole year

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, over a range the system will not render at once.

steps.note: Emitted as asked. The API returns RANGE_TOO_LONG (E4) on the success path.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report that the range is too long to render and offer to narrow it — by month, or by quarter. Narrowing is the actor's choice, not the planner's (PR-1 does not apply here; the range came from them).

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on a closed financial period.
resolvedPlans.outcome: The entries come back with period_closed true. Report that it is readable but not postable — reading history is always permitted, changing it is not (PR-4).

intent.name: finance.trialbalance.read
intent.summary: Produce the trial balance as at a date and prove the two columns agree. One step.
routesHere: produce the trial balance as at 30 September

routesHere.text: 30 September tak ka trial balance chahiye
routesHere.gloss: I need the trial balance as at 30 September
do the books balance or not?

routesHere: run the trial balance for the year end

routesElsewhere.note: Where the columns do not agree the difference is shown rather than hidden, because that is the one thing this use case exists to reveal (BR-3).
A budget is a plan set alongside the books, not part of them (UC-04-20 BR-9).

steps.note: One step. The two columns are totalled from what is posted, and where they do not agree the difference is shown rather than hidden (BR-3).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A date before the financial year begins is enforced by the API and arrives as an error. Columns that do not agree are not an error — they are the finding (E2).
plan.atomicity: A read that writes an audit entry, because the trial balance carries the school's whole position (BR-11). Nothing is posted or adjusted. Where the columns disagree the difference is reported, never forced to zero.

operations.name: finance.trialbalance.read
operations.purpose: Return the trial balance as at a date, with both column totals and any difference between them.

parameters.name: as_at_date
parameters.notes: The date the trial balance is produced as at. Not before the financial year begins (E7).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The two columns and whether they agree.

fields.name: rows
fields.description: account, debit, credit — every account with a balance.

fields.name: total_debits
fields.description: The debit column.

fields.name: total_credits
fields.description: The credit column, which must equal it (BR-3).

fields.name: difference
fields.description: Zero where they agree. Shown rather than hidden where they do not (BR-3).

fields.name: balances
fields.description: Whether the two columns agree.

fields.name: produced_at
fields.description: So a figure quoted an hour later can be dated (BR-8).

fields.name: as_at_date
fields.description: What it is produced as at.

fields.name: financial_year
fields.description: The year it runs against (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The two columns do not agree.
errors.written: The audit entry for the read.
errors.note: The difference is shown rather than hidden — this is the one thing the trial balance exists to reveal (BR-3), so it is a finding rather than a failure.

errors.meaning: The date falls before the financial year begins.

operations.writesOnRead: Producing a trial balance writes an audit entry, because it carries the school's whole financial position (BR-11).

planningRules.rule: Never total the columns yourself, and never reconcile them in a reply. Both come from what is posted, and a figure worked out anywhere else is a second set of books.

Report a difference as the finding, not as a failure. Where the columns do not agree the difference is shown rather than hidden, because that is the one thing this use case exists to reveal (BR-3) — and it means something is wrong in the books, which somebody needs to know.
Never offer to adjust anything to make it balance. Nothing is posted here (BR-4), and an adjusting entry that forces agreement hides exactly what the trial balance was run to find.
Quote it with its produced_at and its as-at date. A trial balance quoted in a meeting an hour later has to be datable (BR-8), and the two dates are different things.

request.text: 30 September tak ka trial balance nikaalo
request.gloss: produce the trial balance as at 30 September

resolvedPlans.outcome: Both columns totalling PKR 8,412,900 with a difference of zero, produced at 08-09-2026 10:14. Quote both dates — the as-at date and when it was produced (PR-4).

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, where debits exceed credits by PKR 4,000.

steps.note: Emitted unchanged. The API returns COLUMNS_DISAGREE (E2) on the success path.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Report the difference of PKR 4,000 plainly as a finding: something is wrong in the books. Never offer to adjust it away (PR-3) — the correction is a voucher or a reversal use case, and finding it is the next piece of work.

request.text: pichle financial year se pehle ka trial balance dikhao
request.gloss: show the trial balance from before the last financial year

steps.note: Emitted as stated. The API returns BEFORE_FINANCIAL_YEAR (E7).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is produced. Report that the date falls before the financial year begins — and note that the financial year is not the academic session and is defined nowhere in the specification (PR-5 of the ledger contract).

intent.name: finance.voucher.trace
intent.summary: Trace a ledger entry back to what caused it — the invoice, the payment, the correction or the voucher, and from there to the student or supplier behind it. One step.

routesHere.gloss: where did this entry come from?

routesHere.text: is voucher ke peeche kya hai?

routesHere: trace this ledger line back to its source

routesElsewhere.note: A correction is a further voucher, never a change to a line in the ledger (BR-5).
Tracing reaches the student; opening their record is a separate act.

steps.note: One step. Every entry can be traced to what caused it, and from there to the student, supplier or payment behind it — an entry nobody can trace is an entry nobody can defend (BR-6).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A source document that has since been deactivated is reported rather than hidden.
plan.atomicity: A read that writes an audit entry (BR-11). Nothing is posted or changed.

operations.name: finance.voucher.trace
operations.purpose: Return what caused a ledger entry and the record behind it.

parameters.name: entry_id

resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with account, date, amount and source type.

parameters.notes: The ledger entry, resolved from how the actor named it — the voucher number, or the account, date and amount.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: What caused the entry, and what lies behind that.

fields.name: entry_id
fields.description: The entry.

fields.name: source_type
fields.description: Invoice, payment, correction, voucher, credit, write-off or refund (BR-4).

fields.name: source_reference
fields.description: The invoice number, receipt number or voucher number.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: The student, household or supplier behind it (BR-6).

fields.name: raised_by
fields.description: Who caused it, and when.

fields.name: approved_by
fields.description: Who approved it, where the source required approval.

fields.name: source_deactivated
fields.description: True where the source document has since been deactivated (E5). Reported, not hidden.

errors.meaning: The source document has been deactivated.
errors.written: The audit entry for the read.
errors.note: The entry still traces to it. A deactivated source is reported, because an entry nobody can trace is an entry nobody can defend (BR-6).

operations.writesOnRead: Tracing an entry writes an audit entry, because it reaches the student, household or supplier behind the money (BR-11).

planningRules.rule: Never infer a source. Every entry carries what caused it (BR-6), and a guess about which invoice a figure came from is exactly the kind of thing the trace exists to make unnecessary.
Report a deactivated source as deactivated. The entry still traces to it, and hiding that leaves a figure nobody can account for (BR-6, E5).
Never offer to correct the entry. A correction is a voucher or one of the reversal use cases, never a change to a ledger line (BR-5).
Never chain a read of the student or supplier record. Tracing reaches them; opening their record is a separate act with its own permissions.

request.text: ye 5000 ki entry kahan se aayi?
request.gloss: where did this 5000 entry come from?

resolvedPlans.outcome: The entry traces to receipt RCP/LHR/2026/0417 against Ayesha Khan's September invoice, recorded by Accounts on 08-09-2026. Report the chain as given — never infer it (PR-1).

request.text: is voucher ke peeche kya hai?

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, on a hand-entered payment voucher.
resolvedPlans.outcome: It traces to a payment voucher, its payee, its description and who approved it. Where the voucher carries a supporting document, that is what an auditor asks for (UC-04-19 BR-12).

resolvedPlans.context: Accounts, Johar Town branch, where the source invoice was cancelled.
resolvedPlans.outcome: It traces to the cancelled invoice, with source_deactivated true. Report that plainly (PR-2) — the entry still stands in the books, and the cancellation posted its own balancing entry alongside it.
